Highest compounding, lowest cost, unblocks everything. |

| 13 | W3.16 `mag.cmd realign`, W3.17 FRAMEWORK_LOAD, W3-addition verdicts panel + gap-sentinel | 7 | If time | Operator-facing; zero downstream dependencies; safe to slip. |

**Cuts (dropped from 7 days):** W3.15 clone-burn compaction (cache-hit gains are speculative, UNPROVEN; no other item depends on it), W2-addition print-the-next-clone-without-the-scars (endemic-rules rail is a real fix but touches the accept path; doing it under deadline risks the batch-accept bypass it's meant to kill), and W3.17 FRAMEWORK_LOAD regeneration (nice-to-have; "front door can never be stale" is cosmetic until real users exist, UNPROVEN value). W3.13's full duel harness may degrade to "retro-judge G1/G3 only" if Day 6 slips.

The plan's own ranking is wrong in one structural way: it puts WAVE 0 first but keeps Wave 1 before Wave 2, when the canary (W2.6) and zero-collect detector (W2.8) should land *inside* Wave 1, not after it. The doc's "GATES THAT DON'T WATCH THEMSELVES" disease means every Wave-1 wiring lands unverified unless the watchers go first or concurrent; wiring organs into a metabolism you cannot observe recreates "write-only everything" at the integration layer. Second disagreement: W1.2 (dual-mode client) is sequenced as item 2 in the doc but is actually the riskiest Wave-1 item (forces the flock determinism fix, per its own text), so it belongs last in the wave, after the transport and protocol it depends on. The doc's "waves 1-2 are small diffs... days, not weeks" claim is credible for Wave 2 but optimistic for W1.2; that single item is where the 7-day budget most likely breaks.

## Kills

**1. Section 4.3, T1 CONFIDENCE.** Calibration_state = "verified" requires rolling ECE over m = 50 gated answers per (model, shape), but section 4.1 requires only n_min = 20 to qualify for routing. So a cell can qualify for routing while its confidence trigger is unverified, meaning T1 is dead code for the first 30 verdicts of every cell's life and every low-confidence event falls through to T4 (a non-climb). Production: cascades stall on low confidence with no escalation path, and the receipt logs a "trigger" that never authorizes anything. Worse, ECE over gated answers conflates gate pass-rate with confidence calibration; a model that is confidently wrong 50% of the time on G0 gates has decent ECE and terrible routing fitness. The spec never defines how confidence scores are captured or stored; there is no column for them in section 2. UNPROVEN whether the m = 50 window is even reachable for long-tail shapes at the section 4.4 probe budget of 0.50 USD/week.

**2. Section 2, capability table vs. section 3.1 G3 cap.** The G3 CAP is stated as a hard routing rule but the schema has no way to enforce it atomically. gate_class_mix is a JSON blob; passes/fails are pre-blended weighted aggregates with no per-class decomposition. When a cell gains its first G0 verdict, there is no specified recomputation: does the cap lift retroactively, does eff_lb95 change, does the router see it this request or next rebuild? "Rebuildable by replay" (section 2) is hand-waving; replay ordering under concurrent verdict writes is unspecified, and SQLite with no WAL mode or write serialization stated means two principals writing verdicts to the same cell can produce divergent chain heads (prev_sha256 collision), which per the quarantine rule silently zeroes routing authority for that cell. Production: the single most important invariant (chain integrity) has no concurrency story.

**3. Section 3.2, RECUSAL RULE.** "Principal family (rotation lineage via rotated_from)" only covers key rotation. Nothing covers: two principals run by the same operator (the funded judgment lane judging cells it "does not operate" is enforced only by self-declared operator identity, which the schema does not record at all; principal has no operator field). Production: one operator registers two principal_ids with disjoint rotated_from chains, self-judges G3 on its own fleet, and every verdict is chain-valid and signature-valid. The separation-of-duties check on receipt_ref is the only computable rule; the recusal rule as written is unenforceable from the schema given. Also UNPROVEN: expires_utc "fail closed when passed" has no specified comparison clock (writer clock vs. verifier clock skew).

## Five missing test predicates

1. **Chain fork detection:** FOR any two verdict rows sharing a prev_sha256 (other than genesis), the ledger MUST reject the later-inserted row AND quarantine dependent capability rows; replay MUST be deterministic under interleaved writes. (Section 2 asserts rebuildability; no test pins it.)

2. **G3 cap transition:** FOR a cell with n >= n_min composed entirely of G3 verdicts, eff_lb95 presented to the router MUST be < threshold; AND after insertion of one G0 verdict, the next router read MUST reflect the uncapped value without a manual rebuild step. (Section 3.1 hard rule, no transition semantics.)

3. **Decay monotonicity vs. probe injection:** FOR a stale cell (T4 fired, probe scheduled), insertion of k = 5 fresh G0 verdicts MUST move eff_lb95 monotonically and MUST NOT demote a previously qualifying cell below threshold if the fresh verdicts all pass. (Section 4.1 "freshness is re-earned"; the blend formula can still demote with 5 passes if prior lb95 was low; spec never checks this interaction.)

4. **Idempotency under replay:** FOR a verdict replayed with identical (receipt_ref, gate_id) but different verdict value, the ledger MUST reject AND log; FOR identical full row, MUST accept as no-op with unchanged chain head. (UNIQUE constraint rejects both cases identically; a hostile replayer cannot distinguish attack from retry, and neither can the audit log.)

5. **T2 advisory invariant:** FOR any request while C_rework is unmeasured, the receipt MUST contain T2 fields (P(fail_i), P(fail_j), prices) AND the routing decision MUST be byte-identical to a run with T2 disabled. (Section 4.2 demotion "logs but does not fire" is untestable without a differential predicate; also guards against the arithmetic leaking into selection before the harness measures C_rework.)

# Grade

## Fabrication check

No DIGEST.md was provided, so every number is UNPROVEN against source. Internal consistency check:

- **Sixteen logos**: the essay names fifteen (Conductor, Vorflux, opencode, Kilo, Vercel, warp, Lovable, T3, Dactyl, Notion, NOUS, OpenClaw, Hyperagent, Devin, Playhouse). The sixteenth is never named. Playhouse itself is flagged "unconfirmed." The count is asserted, not demonstrated.
- **Collusion odds ("What we already hold")**: "one chance in two for copied pairs of claims, one in six for three." If claims are binary and independent, three matching claims is 1-in-4, not 1-in-6. Either the claims aren't binary (unstated), the fingerprint isn't uniform (unstated), or the number is wrong. UNPROVEN and internally suspicious.
- **"Best 2026 result on tiered delegation" ("GPS is the keystone")**: no paper name, no venue, no number for the score that "did not move." A load-bearing citation with zero traceable identifiers. UNPROVEN, highest fabrication risk in the document.
- **"Ninety percent subsidized by your own cloud credits"**: 90% is a precise figure attached to a vague mechanism. UNPROVEN.
- **"Two hundred two out of two hundred two green"**: a 100% pass rate on 202 tapes is itself a red flag — either the tapes are trivial or the check is. The essay treats it as proof, not as a smell.
- **"D1 through D7"**: seven decisions referenced with no content. UNPROVEN.
- **Word count (1197) and em-dash count (0)**: em-dash claim verified against the pasted text — correct. Word count plausible, not independently verified.

## Power score: 6/10

Strong: the "meter as the missing organ" frame is a real gap claim; the self-confessed birth defects in "GPS is the keystone" are the most credible passage in the document; the climb order is sequenced with stated reasons. Weak: the essay's confidence outruns its receipts everywhere it cites external reality. It preaches "route on receipts, not labels" while routing its own argument on unlabeled citations.

## Three weakest claims

1. **"The research lane checked and found the seat empty" ("The house behind the slide")** — an absence-of-competitors claim with no search method, no scope, no date. This is the entire thesis and it rests on an unverifiable negative.
2. **The unnamed 2026 ablation ("GPS is the keystone")** — "a fifth of the cost per solve," "the score did not move": no identifiers, and it conveniently inverts the essay's own product (the router) into a non-keystone. Suspiciously well-fitted.
3. **"Nobody else's platform can say that sentence" / "the only meter in the market" ("What we already hold")** — absolute market claims stacked on the same unproven absence search. Also: "provable play" via frozen tapes proves the play was recorded, not that it was honest.

## Do the three dumb rules survive hostile reading?

- **Rule 1 (route on receipts, not labels)**: Survives. Mechanically checkable, and the "marketing is not a row" clause closes the obvious loophole. Strongest of the three.
- **Rule 2 (no verdict without evidence bytes)**: Partially survives. It kills trivial inflation but not adversarial inflation — a garbage tape hash or a rigged test run is still "checkable artifact" bytes. The rule binds verdicts to *existence* of evidence, not *validity* of evidence. A hostile reader routes garbage through it on day one.
- **Rule 3 (same row everywhere)**: Weakest under hostility. Its load-bearing premise — "The GPS schema and the game payload already share it" — is UNPROVEN, and unifying schemas across model-eval, agent-play, and game-round semantics is where "one grammar" claims historically die (verdict semantics differ across all three). As written it's an aspiration wearing a law's clothing.

## Summary judgment

The document's central virtue — confessing the ledger's birth defects — is also its central exposure: it admits pass-rates are inflatable and evidence unverified, then asks the reader to trust 202/202 green, 28 and 41 tests, and a 1-in-6 fingerprint on the same unverified footing. The meter does not yet meter itself.
reasoning_tail:
.

Dumb rules hostile reading: Rule 1 survives as checkable. Rule 2 survives mechanically but "checkable artifact" — tape hash can be garbage; evidence bytes ≠ evidence validity; partially survives. Rule 3: "GPS schema and game payload already share it" UNPROVEN; grammar unification is aspirational.

## Structural problem before any rating

The instrument is pointed at its own commissioner. The operator asked for a persona to "extract and replicate," and the estate that depends on him produced the profile. Every "receipt" passed through an operator-approved gate: operator-corrections SKILL is his compiled self-corrections, OPERATOR_CANON_TRIAGE ran his own posts through his own estate's gate, FLEET_IMPRINT quotes were selected by the fleet. This is a man's self-model laundered through citations. The doc's honesty spine disclaimer does not cure selection bias; it just labels it.

## Where the flattery lives

**AGREEABLENESS, LOW-MED "with high loyalty"** is the worst offender. The loyalty claim rests on five approval quotes ("stamp it bad ass," "holy shit Lillith") pulled from 4,968 messages, under 0.1% sampling, with no method stated and no base rate of neutral or cold messages for contrast. The headline itself, "challenging is the affection," is the estate's interpretive frame, not the operator's, and it is exactly the hagiographic move: re-reading profane correction as love. Law 12 ("THE STANDARD BINDS BOTH WAYS") is self-authored doctrine about himself. A man's stated ideal is not evidence he practices it.

**EXTRAVERSION, MED "asymmetric"** flatters by reframing. 4,968 messages are messages to machines. That is usage, not interpersonal bandwidth. The Nacho section is pure sentiment: a dog story and a house name are narrative, not measurement, and the doc admits the medical history is on record then uses the emotional content anyway. "Performs publicly, connects narrowly, deeply" has no receipt for "deeply" at all. The "deep" connection cited is with the fleet, i.e., with the instrument writing the profile.

**NEUROTICISM, "structured regulation"** is a flattering spin on thin data. One veto (law 15) and one accepted reframe on 2026-09-20 are two instances. Thu/Fri peaks are indistinguishable from a work calendar. The UNPROVEN ledger on anxiety is correct, but the rating label still smuggles in "self-aware" and "regulates," which are character virtues, not observations.

**OPENNESS, HIGH** leans on law 10, "NO SACRED COWS," which is his self-description. The cross-domain list (mRNA, mycology, Go, shadertoy) is topic-hopping; the same evidence is cited elsewhere in the doc as LOW-side conscientiousness (35 abandoned prototypes). The model double-counts one behavior as two virtues. "No authority worship" is UNPROVEN: nothing in the cited corpus shows him deferring to or defying a live external authority, only text consumption.

## What the data does not support

- Any interpersonal behavior. Zero cited human-to-human interaction outside public broadcast. Every "connection" receipt is operator-to-fleet.
- The warmth base rate. No count of approval vs. correction vs. neutral messages across the 4,968.
- "Wants to be outsmarted." One succession-inversion line plus a self-written law.
- The deterministic diff. The doc admits fingerprint(text) is "one command away" and was not run. The one check that would constrain all five ratings was available and skipped.
- Any counter-evidence ledger. The only negative datum in the entire profile is the 35-prototypes admission, and it comes from the estate's own self-assessment file, which itself reads as performed humility.

## The rating I would change

AGREEABLENESS: drop to LOW, strike "high loyalty," mark loyalty UNPROVEN. The LOW-MED rating is defensible on the correction register alone. The "with high loyalty" qualifier and the headline framing exist to make the profanity legible as affection, which is the profile's stated surprise and its clearest hagiography. Loyalty requires evidence of behavior toward others across time under cost; the corpus contains none. Until the fingerprint run and a message-register base rate exist, the honest rating is LOW with a note that warmth frequency is unmeasured, not LOW-MED with a virtue attached.
reasoning_tail:
OW with loyalty UNPROVEN, or drop the loyalty qualifier. Alternatively Extraversion: 4,968 messages to AI agents is not interpersonal bandwidth; the dog story is sentiment. I'll pick Agreeableness - the headline axis is the flattery axis.

Format: no em-dashes, cite sections, no praise, no preamble.

# Experiment Design: Lattice-Projected Tiny Transformer for Water-Graph Legality

## 1. Task Domain: WATER-GRAPH LEGALITY

**Instance.** A directed graph `G = (V, E, τ)` with node types `{source, sink, junction}` and edge types `τ(e) ∈ {pipe, gate, pump}`. Each edge holds one state from a typed finite set:

| Edge type | States |
|---|---|
| pipe | `empty`, `flowing` |
| gate | `closed`, `open-empty`, `open-flowing` |
| pump | `off`, `on-flowing` |

**Action.** `a ∈ {open(gate), close(gate), turn-on(pump), turn-off(pump)}` applied to a current state `s`.

**Query.** Classify `(G, s, a)` into one of:
- `ILLEGAL` — action violates a precondition (wrong edge type, pump-on without upstream pressure, closing a gate that is the sole supply to a pressurized junction, …)
- `LEGAL-NOT-WINNING` — action applies but post-state does not satisfy the goal
- `WINNING` — post-state satisfies goal: **every sink edge is `flowing`** at the propagator fixpoint.

**Distribution.** Train: `|V| ∈ [4,12]`, `|E| ≈ 1.5|V|`, edge types sampled with all combos seen. OOD test splits: (a) `|V| ∈ [13,20]`, (b) held-out topology motifs (e.g., no pumps at all during training, pumps at test), (c) *near-miss adversarial*: legal action on a graph, plus the same graph with one edge retyped so the action becomes illegal (forces symbolic, not pattern, matching).

## 2. Lattice Definition

**Atoms.** `A = { (e, σ) : e ∈ E, σ ∈ States(τ(e)) }` — the *legal typed edge-states* (type-consistent pairs; `(pipe, closed)` is not an atom). `|A| = Σ_e |States(τ(e))|`, typically 20–40.

**Lattice.** `L = (2^A, ⊆)` with join `∪`, meet `∩`, ⊥ = ∅, ⊤ = A. A *state* is an element `S ∈ 2^A` with exactly one atom per edge (a complete assignment). A *domain* is any element of L (a set of candidate states per edge).

**Propagator (closure/narrowing operator).** `P : 2^A → 2^A`, monotone, contracting (`P(S) ⊆ S`), idempotent. Rules (implemented as domain-narrowing, CSP arc-consistency style):

1. **R1 (source flow):** a source-adjacent edge may only be `flowing`/`open-flowing`/`on-flowing` if the source is active; otherwise those states are removed.
2. **R2 (forward reachability):** edge `e` may be in a flowing state only if there exists a directed path from an active source to `e` where every edge's domain intersects the flowing states. Otherwise remove flowing states from `D_e`.
3. **R3 (pump precondition):** pump `on-flowing` requires its upstream edge's domain ∩ flowing ≠ ∅; else remove `on-flowing`.
4. **R4 (junction conservation):** if all in-edges of junction `v` have domains ⊆ non-flowing states, remove flowing states from all out-edges of `v`. If any out-edge is definitely flowing, remove the all-non-flowing combination from in-edges (i.e., at least one in-edge must retain a flowing state).
5. **R5 (gate blocking):** a `closed` gate removes flowing states from all downstream edges not reachable via another open path (subsumed by R2 if reachability treats `closed` as blocked).

`P` is applied to fixpoint: `P^ω(S)`. **Contradiction** = some `D_e = ∅` after fixpoint.

**Ground truth (supervision source):**
- Apply action `a` as a domain restriction on `s` (e.g., `close(g)` forces `D_g = {closed}`).
- Run `P^ω`. If any domain empties → `ILLEGAL`.
- Else if every sink-adjacent edge's domain = `{flowing}` (forced) → `WINNING`.
- Else → `LEGAL-NOT-WINNING`.

This makes the propagator the *single* oracle: labels, dense per-edge targets (the fixpoint domains), and the trace of eliminations are all derived from it. The propagator is ~50 lines of code, `O((V+E)·iters)` per call, trivially exact — so the experiment tests whether the *model* internalizes it, not whether the oracle is right.

## 3. Model (~1M params)

**Backbone.** Transformer: `d_model=128`, 4 layers, 4 heads, MLP `4×`, pre-LN, RoPE or learned pos. Parameter budget: 4 × (65K attn + 131K MLP) ≈ 786K + token embeddings (~100K, shared input/output) + heads ≈ **~0.95M**.

**Input serialization.** Graph as token sequence, ≤256 tokens: `[node-type tokens; edge tokens (u, v, τ, current-state); ACTION token; SEP]`. Edge states use the atom vocabulary (size |A| + specials).

**Two passes with lattice projection:**
1. **Pass 1:** backbone → per-edge logits `z_e ∈ R^{|States(τ(e))|}` → soft domains `p_e = softmax(z_e)`.
2. **Lattice projection π:** hard assignment `ĥ_e = onehot(argmax z_e)`; run propagator `P^ω` on the hard domains → survival mask `M_{e,σ} ∈ {0,1}`. Pass-2 input per edge: `M ⊙ p_e` renormalized (mask treated as constant — **straight-through**; gradient flows through `p_e`). If `P^ω` empties a domain, emit a `CONTRADICTION` token for that edge (this is the abstain pathway's main input).
3. **Pass 2:** same backbone weights, second forward over `[original tokens with projected state tokens]` → pooled representation → **4-way head: {illegal, legal-not-winning, winning, ABSTAIN}**.

**Training.** AdamW, lr 3e-4, cosine, 20K steps, batch 256, bf16, 5 seeds. Losses:
- CE on 3-way label (abstain logit masked out on normal examples).
- Dense auxiliary loss: KL(`p_e` ‖ fixpoint-domain target distribution) — this is where propagator supervision enters.
- **Abstain supervision:** label ABSTAIN on examples where (a) the projected fixpoint leaves domain size > 1 on any edge (propagator under-determined → model shouldn't guess), or (b) the 3-way head was wrong on a held-out mini-batch in a previous epoch (self-distilled hardness). At eval, abstain is also triggered by `p(abstain) > τ` swept for the risk–coverage curve.

## 4. Abstain-Adjusted Soundness Metric

Let `c` be an abstain threshold. Over the test set:

- **Coverage(c)** = fraction of examples answered (not abstained).
- **Soundness(c)** = accuracy on answered examples = `correct / (correct + wrong)`.
- **AAS (primary scalar)** = area under the Soundness–Coverage curve, ∫₀¹ Soundness(c) dCoverage(c). Report Soundness@{50%, 90%, 95%} coverage as checkpoints.

**Soundness decomposition (the LDT-specific claim):** partition non-abstained *errors* by whether the projected lattice element was (i) contradictory (propagator flagged ⊥ but head answered anyway) or (ii) consistent-but-wrong (head overrode a sound projection). The paper's claim to test: **with projection + abstain, errors concentrate in category (ii) at near-zero rate, and category (i) ≈ 0** — i.e., unsound answers occur only when the mechanism had the information to abstain. Report `U = unsound-error rate at coverage 0.9`; target `U < 0.1%`.

Also report **exact-match of projected domains vs. propagator fixpoint** (intermediate-task accuracy) — necessary condition for the soundness story.

## 5. Controls

| # | Control | What it isolates |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Same model, single pass, no projection, no abstain | Full-mechanism contribution |
| C2 | Two passes, no projection (re-encode pass-1 output) | Extra compute/depth |
| C3 | Two passes, projection with **shuffled/wrong constraint set** (R2–R4 randomized) | Constraints vs. generic bottleneck |
| C4 | Projection, no abstain head | Abstain contribution |
| C5 | Abstain, no projection | Abstain alone |
| C6 | Single-pass model at matched FLOPs (8 layers, ~2M params) | Scale vs. mechanism |
| C7 | Full model, label-only supervision (no dense propagator loss) | Value of propagator supervision |
| C8 | Full model, soft projection only (no hard straight-through) | Discreteness |

All controls share data, steps, seeds, and the metric suite. C3 is the critical falsifier: if wrong constraints match the full model, the "lattice" is just an information bottleneck.

## 6. Compute Estimate

- **Data:** 5M train / 200K per test split. Generation: propagator ≈ 0.1–0.5 ms/example (Python; 10× faster in Rust) → 5M × 0.3 ms ≈ 25 min on 16 cores. Storage ~2 GB (tokenized, uint16).
- **Training:** 20K steps × 256 batch × 256 tokens ≈ 1.3B tokens; two passes doubles forward cost → FLOPs ≈ 6 · 10⁶ · 1.3B · 1.5 ≈ 1.2 × 10¹⁶. On one A100 (40% MFU, bf16) ≈ **8 minutes of pure compute; ~1–2 h wall-clock per run with overhead**.
- **Total:** 9 configurations × 5 seeds = 45 runs ≈ **45–90 GPU-hours; ≤ 4 GPU-days, ~$50–150 on cloud**. Well under one GPU-week — kill on overrun at 3× this.

## 7. Kill Criteria

Abort the line (or report null result) if any hold at the pre-registered evaluation:

1. **Mechanism-null:** C1 (plain single-pass) achieves AAS within 1% of the full model on the in-distribution test — projection + abstain add nothing.
2. **Constraint-null:** C3 (wrong lattice) matches the full model's AAS within 1% — projection is a compute artifact, not symbolic.
3. **Soundness failure:** `U > 1%` at coverage 0.9, or Soundness@0.9 < 98% in-distribution (propagator is 100% by construction; a 1M model should get near this on 12-node graphs).
4. **No abstain structure:** risk–coverage curve is flat (abstain head uncorrelated with errors; AUC of error-vs-abstain-logit < 0.6).
5. **No OOD transfer:** Soundness@0.5-coverage on the 13–20-node split < 90%, or near-miss adversarial split < 90% at any coverage.
6. **Training pathology:** straight-through projection diverges (loss NaN or >2× baseline loss) in ≥ 3/5 seeds; or full model needs > 5× the data of C1 to match C1's accuracy.
7. **Budget:** > 3× compute estimate or > 2 weeks calendar.

If 1–2 pass but 5 fails, the honest finding is "lattice projection helps in-distribution soundness but not generalization" — worth reporting, not extending.

## 8. Implementation Order

1. Propagator + labeler + unit tests (contradiction cases hand-checked on ~50 graphs). *(1 day)*
2. Data generator + splits + near-miss generator. *(1 day)*
3. Backbone, single-pass baseline (C1) — establishes floor. *(2 days)*
4. Projection layer (mask plumbing, CONTRADICTION tokens) + two-pass wiring. *(2–3 days)*
5. Abstain head + metric harness (risk–coverage sweep, decomposition). *(1 day)*
6. Controls C2–C8, 5 seeds each, aggregate. *(compute-bound)*

The single cleanest falsifiable claim to pre-register: **at matched parameters and FLOPs, the lattice-projected two-pass model with an abstain head achieves ≥ 99% soundness at 90% coverage with unsound-error rate < 0.1%, while every control without both components fails at least one of these thresholds.**
reasoning_tail:
experiment design with multiple deliverables "concrete enough to implement." I'll use markdown headers, code-ish definitions, tables where useful. Length: substantial but not bloated — maybe 1200–1800 words. Include pseudocode for propagator and projection. Avoid excessive hedging.

Let me write it.
